stem: Write structures of different chain isomers of alkanes corresponding to the molecular formula \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\). Also write their IUPAC names.

Write structures of different isomeric alkyl groups corresponding to the molecular formula \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\). Write IUPAC names of alcohols obtained by attachment of \(-\text{OH}\) groups at different carbons of the chain.
solution:
| Structure of \(-\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\) group | Corresponding alcohol | Name of alcohol |
|---|---|---|
| (i) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}\) | Pentan-1-ol |
| (ii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(-)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) (free valency at C-2) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) | Pentan-2-ol |
| (iii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(-)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) (free valency at C-3) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) | Pentan-3-ol |
| (iv) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}\) | 3-Methylbutan-1-ol |
| (v) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}\) | 2-Methylbutan-1-ol |
| (vi) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(-)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) (free valency at C-2) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) | 2-Methylbutan-2-ol |
| (vii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2-\) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\) | 2,2-Dimethylpropan-1-ol |
| (viii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(-)-\text{CH}_3\) (free valency at C-2 of the butane chain) | \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3\) | 3-Methylbutan-2-ol |
_note: The book prints each alkyl group as a skeletal structure with the free valency shown as a dangling bond; that dangling bond is rendered here as a trailing dash or a parenthetical statement of which carbon carries it.

stem:
Write structures for each of the following compounds. Why are the given names incorrect? Write correct IUPAC names.

(i) 2-Ethylpentane

(ii) 5-Ethyl-3-methylheptane
solution:
(i) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)

The longest chain is of six carbon atoms and not of five. Hence, the correct name is 3-Methylhexane.

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)

Numbering is to be started from the end which gives the lower number to the ethyl group. Hence, the correct name is 3-Ethyl-5-methylheptane.

stem: Calculate number of sigma (\(\sigma\)) and pi (\(\pi\)) bonds in the above structures (i-iv).

solution:

stem: Write structures and IUPAC names of different structural isomers of alkenes corresponding to \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\).

Draw cis and trans isomers of the following compounds. Also write their IUPAC names :

(i) \(\text{CHCl}=\text{CHCl}\)

(ii) \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CCH}_3=\text{CCH}_3\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\)
solution:
(i) With both H atoms on the same side of the double bond (and hence both Cl atoms on the same side) the isomer is cis-1,2-dichloroethene; with one H and one Cl on each side of the double bond the isomer is trans-1,2-dichloroethene.

(ii) With both \(\text{CH}_3\) groups on the same side of the double bond (and both \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) groups on the other side) the isomer is cis-3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene; with one \(\text{CH}_3\) and one \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) on each side the isomer is trans-3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene.
_note: The book gives the solution as four drawn structures with the two groups written above and below each doubly bonded carbon; the arrangement is stated here in words, with the book's own IUPAC names retained verbatim.

Write structures of different isomers corresponding to the 5th member of alkyne series. Also write IUPAC names of all the isomers. What type of isomerism is exhibited by different pairs of isomers?
solution:
The 5th member of the alkyne series has the molecular formula \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\). The possible isomers are:

(a) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) — Hex-1-yne

(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) — Hex-2-yne

(c) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) — Hex-3-yne

(d) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) — 3-Methylpent-1-yne

(e) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3\) — 4-Methylpent-1-yne

(f) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3\) — 4-Methylpent-2-yne

(g) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_3\) — 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-yne

Position and chain isomerism are shown by different pairs.

stem: How will you convert ethanoic acid into benzene?
solution:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH(aq)}} \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Soda lime}} \text{CH}_4 \xrightarrow[h\nu]{\text{Cl}_2} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}\)

\(\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{Wurtz reaction}]{\text{Na/dry ether}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2\)

\(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2} \text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CHBr} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNH}_2} \text{CH}\equiv\text{CH}\)

\(3\,\text{CH}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow[873\,\text{K}]{\text{Red hot iron tube}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\) (benzene)

(c) the bond-line structure shown in the figure

(d) a benzene ring bearing the chain \(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\)

_note: Sub-items (c), (d) and (e) are printed as drawn structures. (d) and (e) are stated in words here because they are unambiguous; (c) is a bare bond-line drawing and is carried as a figure so the question stays answerable without describing it.
